sessionReviewRoots runs REVIEW_PACKAGE_PATH with matchAll over the content of every history message and every tool-call argument. The pattern opens with an unanchored lazy class `[^\s"'`<>|;&()]*?` that must be followed by the literal `.metaproject`. On a run of L characters with no whitespace/quote/delimiter and no `.metaproject`, every start position scans forward to the end of the run before failing, so one scan costs O(L^2). Attack vector: the author of the PR under review adds a long unbroken token (a minified bundle, a base64 fixture, a single-line JSON/SVG with no spaces or quotes, a long URL) to a file in the PR; the reviewing agent reads the diff or the file, the tool result is pushed into `history`, and from then on holdReviewGate (src/commands/agent.ts:3487) calls sessionReviewRoots(history, process.cwd()) on every turn end of a session that has run `keryx review ...`. A 100 KB token is ~5e9 regex steps, a 1 MB token ~5e11, repeated at each stop and up to MAX_REVIEW_GATE_CONTINUES times.

Extra gate roots are taken from any message content, including tool results that carry untrusted text (fetched pages, the PR's own files and diff), and absolute paths are accepted unchanged. findReviewGateState then folds closedAt from every root into one value and returns null (gate released) when any root holds a review-flow package closed since session start that is newer than the chosen package's manifest. Separately, an open package another concurrent session opened in a named sibling worktree can be chosen as `best` when cwd has no active pointer, holding this session on the wrong review.

The header states the KERYX_USAGE line wins over the result envelope 'because the host measured it and the reviewer cannot', but the line lives in the same raw file as the reviewer's reply and the last well-formed line wins.
